Second, keep the workout focused in one area. Right now it sometimes has me leave a bench for a single exercise and then come right back. At a busy gym, holding a bench or a hi-lo is hard, so it would help a lot if the app grouped everything for the muscles I’m working in one spot before moving me to the next station.
That small change would make the sessions much easier to follow in a real gym.

title: The App Is OK-ish
body:
Just like the title says. I can see where people would find this app useful. It has promise, but I think the developers rushed the launching. 

The “AI” is nothing really to write home about. I asked it how I could do a completed workout again and it gave me two different answers. 

The lack of Landmine exercises. 

The lack of Kettlebell exercises. 

The feature that allows you to suggest an exercise isn’t all that great because the “post” button is continually grayed out. 

The support from an actual human is atrocious. If you ask the staff a question, they’ll mark the ticket as closed without any explanation or resolution. 

All-in-all, be cautious about using this app. Don’t expect great things and take it for what it’s worth.

title: Great App! One Suggestion
body:
Incredible app, basically a personal trainer in your pocket
I think this app is fantastic and hands down the only workout app I use.

What makes it great:
* For beginners: It takes away all the guesswork if you don’t know where to start or how to structure a routine.

* For experienced lifters: It eliminates decision fatigue. Having the app program your sessions feels just like working with a personal trainer.

* Smart progression: The adaptive weight suggestions (and set tracking) feel incredibly spot on, almost like it reads your notes and adjusts intensity automatically.

Room for improvement / Feature request:
I’d love to see more cardio features integrated down the road like tracking running workouts or custom cardio sessions besides is already there. It’s primarily a strength app and does that exceptionally well, but expanded cardio would make it a complete all-in-one platform.

Bug report for developers:
The only minor issue occurs when using the search tool to swap or replace an exercise. The search occasionally glitches, images overlap, or the app freezes momentarily.

Overall, I wish I’d found this app years ago and can't wait to see how it evolves. Keep up the awesome work!

title: Best strength training app
body:
I’ve been lifting for years and have tried plenty of workout programs and apps, but Gravl has honestly been a game changer. The way it adapts each workout based on your performance is incredible. It pushes you when you’re ready and adjusts when you need it, so every workout feels productive.
I’ve been using it to rebuild my strength while working around some shoulder and back issues, and it’s helped me make consistent progress without feeling like I’m guessing what to do next. I’ve noticed real improvements in my strength, my physique, and my overall confidence in the gym.
The interface is simple, easy to use, and keeps track of everything automatically, which lets me focus on training instead of planning workouts. If you’re looking for an app that takes the guesswork out of strength training and gives you a personalized program that actually works, I can’t recommend Gravl enough. It’s one of the best fitness investments I’ve made.

title: Better than Fit-Bod
body:
I don't typically write reviews, but the progress I've seen with Gravl made me want to share my experience.

For the past three years, I've been consistently working out, lifting weights, and tracking my progress using Fitbod. While it was helpful, I often found myself frustrated because I didn't feel like I was seeing the results I expected from all the effort I was putting in.

About six weeks ago, I decided to switch to Gravl, and the difference has been incredible. In just six weeks, I've seen more noticeable progress than I ever did using Fitbod. 

One of the biggest improvements has been the rest times. Gravl's recommendations feel much more accurate, which has allowed me to recover properly between sets, lift heavier, and push myself more effectively during workouts.


The result has been increased strength, better performance, and visible progress in a surprisingly short amount of time. If you're serious about strength training and tracking your results, Gravl has been a game-changer for me. The only thing I wished is they would count a cardio session as a workout day.

Another issue I’ve had with this method is if I’m tracking on the watch, it “seems to” sync with the phone, but I’ve had whole workouts end and never show up again. Couldn’t get the workout back, and a new workout was formulated. Extremely frustrating. 

Otherwise I love the app. It’s like Fitbod on steroids.

title: A Fresh Take On A Workout Program
body:
I’ve been a long-time Fitbod user for several years, but recently decided to give Gravl a try—and honestly, I’m glad I did. What really sold me was the variety of splits and routines you can choose from, plus the ability to incorporate deload weeks right into the program.

It feels familiar enough that the transition from Fitbod was easy, but Gravl adds the features I’ve been wishing for. The structure, flexibility, and overall flow just fit where I’m at with my training now.

If you’re looking for something that keeps the best parts of Fitbod but gives you more control and smarter programming options, Gravl is absolutely worth the switch.

title: Waste of time

title: Major issues with latest build and watch synchronization
body: Been using this app for over a year and recently it’s been giving me way too many issues. When running the workout from the Apple Watch, it constantly loses connectivity to my iPhone which screws up my session being recorded properly. A few times the app completely crashed my watch and messed up the session. It’s been working great for a while but recent builds have been buggy. I don’t have any other crashes on my Apple Watch outside of when I run this app.

title: Ok but has issues
